ai.description: This small pit viper reaches 40 cm. It is green with faint, dark crossbands and a distinct, triangular head. A pale postocular stripe and reddish-brown tail tip are diagnostic features.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Tropidolaemus huttoni* is best distinguished by its unique, vivid reddish-brown coloration and the presence of a distinct, dark post-ocular stripe that lacks white borders.
ai.habitat: *Tropidolaemus huttoni* inhabits high-altitude evergreen shola forests and grasslands in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations above 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: Hutton’s Pit Viper is primarily nocturnal and exhibits an ambush foraging strategy, remaining motionless on branches to surprise passing prey.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Tropidolaemus huttoni* is viviparous, giving birth to small litters of live young. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: Hutton’s Pit Viper is endemic to the high-elevation shola forests and grasslands of the Western Ghats in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, typically found above 1,500 meters.
